source.title: Partita No. 2 in D minor, BWV 1004 — V. Chaconne

bars.description: The source’s two-quarter opening bar 1, then complete 3/4 bars 2–257 once. The D-major section begins at bar 133, D minor returns at bar 209, and the closing theme at bar 249 is written out; no repeats or arpeggio realisations are invented.

end.basis: MEAS: Final D4 plus its octave/third-harmonic pitch-energy bins (MIDI 62, 74, 81), smoothed over 13 frames at 50 Hz, relative to the 772.2–773.0 s peak, fall from −31.08 dB mean in 778.00–778.25 s to −43.83 dB in 778.25–778.50 s and −47.18 dB in 778.50–778.75 s; subsequent windows remain below −50 dB. Use 778.5 s as a conservative pitched-decay display boundary. Whole-file −45 dB RMS remains active to 782.245 s because of transfer noise. This is not a measured bow release.

endpoints.basis: Pitch-energy overlays identify the opening D4–F4–A4 chord’s leading rise at 2.40 s (peak 2.46 s) and the final D4 reattack at 772.10 s (peak 772.16 s), distinct from the preceding D4 eighth. These windows retain those inspected rises; chord spreading and breath timing are not aural annotations.

engraving.music: \new Staff \with { instrumentName = "Violine" } { \clef treble \key d \minor \time 3/4 \set Score.currentBarNumber = #2 \set Score.internalBarNumber = #2 \partial 2 \melody }

provenance: This is the standalone solo-violin Chaconne, not the whole partita or a piano arrangement. The original source and published MIDI are retained with inventory SHA-256 pins.

The four separately encoded variables melodyOne, melodyTwo, melodyThree and melodyFour are compiled independently. Names identify source variables rather than inferred soprano/alto/bass roles or MIDI channels; their notational voice settings are respectively voiceOne, voiceThree, voiceFive and voiceTwo.

The source sets currentBarNumber to 2 before partial 2 and labels the opening fragment as bar 1. Its 257 source-comment bars occupy 770 quarter units. Source unisons and chord holds remain in their originating variables instead of being truncated by the published merged MIDI staff.

Engraving reuses the immutable source’s complete melody variable and sets both displayed and internal bar counters to 2 before partial 2. LilyPond’s rhythmic-location tags use its internal counter, not currentBarNumber: setting only the original displayed counter mislabels the pickup 0 and the last note 256. The wrapper preserves all notation while making the pickup tag 1 and the final written bar 257; a derived blank box is not a substitute for that final measure.

The arpeggio markings at bars 89 and 201 are not a fully encoded performance realisation. Symbolic sustained chord tones must not be mistaken for Heifetz’s individual string attacks; no notes or repeated arpeggio patterns are fabricated. No aural review or recording-edition identity is claimed.

The final written D4 hold uses an explicit 778.5 s pitch-energy display boundary rather than the noisy whole-file RMS end at 782.245 s. The strongest pitched energy fades around 775 s, with a weak measured tail reaching the documented boundary; neither the display duration nor that threshold is a measured violin release.
